approved: Customs Tariff Amendment (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership Expansion) Bill 2024
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would change Australia's customs duties to reflect the United Kingdom joining the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership.
Goods from the United Kingdom that meet the agreement's origin rules would generally enter Australia duty-free, with some exceptions listed in a schedule.

For certain products, the tariff would be phased down gradually, reaching zero by no later than 1 January 2033, and a safeguard could temporarily restore the previous rate if the United Kingdom keeps its equivalent measure.
Sets a zero customs duty for most goods originating in the United Kingdom.
Creates a phased reduction schedule for some goods, with the final zero rate due by 1 January 2033.
Adds a safeguard clause that can reinstate the pre-Protocol duty rate on certain products while the United Kingdom maintains its own safeguard.
Importers of goods from the United Kingdom and Australian businesses that compete with those imports.
Customs Tariff Amendment (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership Expansion) Act 2024
